# test_hex_to_rgb.py
import pytest

# Adjust this import to match where hex_to_rgb is defined
from your_module import hex_to_rgb


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "hex_value, expected",
    [
        ("#000000", (0, 0, 0)),
        ("#ffffff", (255, 255, 255)),
        ("#FFFFFF", (255, 255, 255)),
        ("#ff0000", (255, 0, 0)),
        ("#00ff00", (0, 255, 0)),
        ("#0000ff", (0, 0, 255)),
        ("#123456", (18, 52, 86)),
        ("abcdef", (171, 205, 239)),  # works without leading #
    ],
)
def test_hex_to_rgb_happy_path(hex_value, expected):
    assert hex_to_rgb(hex_value) == expected


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "hex_value, expected",
    [
        ("##123456", (18, 52, 86)),  # lstrip removes all leading #
        ("#123456789", (18, 52, 86)),  # extra trailing chars are ignored
        ("#12345", (18, 52, 5)),  # final single hex digit is accepted by int()
    ],
)
def test_hex_to_rgb_edge_cases_current_behavior(hex_value, expected):
    assert hex_to_rgb(hex_value) == expected


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "hex_value",
    [
        "",
        "#",
        "#12",
        "#123",
        "#1234",
        "#gg0000",
        "#00xx00",
        "#0000zz",
        "#12-456",
    ],
)
def test_hex_to_rgb_invalid_values_raise_value_error(hex_value):
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        hex_to_rgb(hex_value)


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "value, expected_exception",
    [
        (None, AttributeError),
        (123456, AttributeError),
        (b"#ffffff", TypeError),
    ],
)
def test_hex_to_rgb_non_string_inputs_raise(value, expected_exception):
    with pytest.raises(expected_exception):
        hex_to_rgb(value)
